name: porcelain-trim-audit
title: Audit remaining git-status porcelain call sites for the whole-output-trim first-row bug and fix affected consumers
description: B-b264 (merge 2895bbb5e, v0.3.181) fixed a porcelain-parsing bug class in done-prepare.ts and done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts: a git helper that .trim()s the FULL `git status --porcelain=v1` output strips the first row's leading status column, so the first modified-tracked row (e.g. ' M .lattice/x') parses to a corrupted path ('lattice/x' after slice(3)) and downstream prefix-based material/volatile classification misfires. Untracked '??' rows are immune, so untracked-only test fixtures never catch it. The B-b264 quality reviewer (run B-b264:RR-008) noted other porcelain consumers exist outside that story's scope. A full audit of `grep -rn porcelain packages/main/src` (2026-07-10) found four consumers where the corrupted first row reaches material/volatile classification logic: (1) core/evidence-freshness.ts readMaterialDirtyFiles — full trim + slice(3) feeds isMaterialExcludedPath, so a first-row .lattice metadata change is counted as material dirt inside evidence hash snapshots; (2) handlers/cross-host-review.ts assertMaterialCleanForReview — full trim + slice(3) means a first-row .lattice row misreads as material and false-blocks the cross-host review preflight; (3) handlers/story-query.ts gitPorcelainPaths (via gitOutput full trim) — the story_sync_main dirty preflight filters with isVolatileRuntimeArtifactPath on a corrupted first-row path and can false-block sync; (4) core/partial-done-recovery.ts assertMainWorktreeClean — git() full trim feeds materialStatusLines/statusLinePath, so a first-row volatile runtime artifact is counted as material and done_recover falsely refuses. Two further sites corrupt display-only output (handlers/session.ts readGitStatus brief rows; handlers/story-query.ts DONE-residue status text). All other porcelain call sites were audited and are safe (per-line trimEnd, count-only or emptiness-only usage, bounded-path emptiness checks, or `git worktree list --porcelain` whose rows never start with a space). This story fixes the affected consumers using the raw-read pattern established by B-b264 (gitStatusRows in handlers/done-prepare.ts, gitRaw in core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts), adds first-row modified-tracked regression assertions (pattern: assertModifiedTrackedPathExactness in tasks/done-prepare-merge-rerun-smoke.ts), and records the per-site audit verdict so the next consumer author can see which helpers are safe to copy.
